newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan not to change foreign policy.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan not to change foreign policy.

text.p: Pakistan said on Thursday its basic principles of foreign policy would not be altered despite the ouster of the government of Benazir Bhutto two days ago.
A Foreign Ministry spokesman told reporters that Islamabad would abide by all international agreements and commitments made by the previous government.

"Basic principles of Pakistan's foreign policy would remain unaltered," he said, recalling a similar assurance given by President Farooq Leghari on Tuesday after sacking Bhutto on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
The spokesman said Pakistan would continue to provide "moral, political and diplomatic support" for Moslem militants fighting Indian rule over two-thirds of the disputed Himalayan region of Kashmir.

But he said Islamabad would also continue its quest for peace and stability in the region, a reference to efforts for a negotiated settlement of the dispute with India over Kashmir, one third of which is controlled by Pakistan.
The spokesman said Pakistan had an abiding interest in peace and stability in Afghanistan.
"We shall continue to extend full support to the efforts of the United Nations and the OIC (Organisation of the Islamic Conference)," he said.
Pakistan would attend an international conference on Afghanistan called in New York for November 18 by U.N. Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, he added.

"Pakistan will also make concerted efforts to consolidate and deepen its relations with the Moslem countries and the countries in our neighbourhood in Central Asia," he said, adding that it would try to cement relations with "friends like China and the United States".
